assessment.summary: ABL1 is one of the best-validated oncology drug targets in human medicine, with 7 approved kinase inhibitors (including imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib, and bosutinib), over 5,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and 85 high-resolution crystal structures — several with sub-ångström resolution. The literature base is extensive (>1,200 publications) with strong disease validation in CML and Ph+ ALL. Druggability is unambiguously high across all evidence dimensions.
evidence_gaps: AlphaFold mean pLDDT is only 63.4 (high-confidence fraction 46%), reflecting disordered regions (e.g., N-terminal cap, linker regions) not covered by crystal structures — though this does not impair druggability assessment given the wealth of experimental structures
Resistance mutation landscape (e.g., T315I gatekeeper) continues to evolve; third- and fourth-generation inhibitor coverage may be incomplete in ChEMBL
Selectivity profiles across the kinome are not fully characterised for all 5,295 compounds in ChEMBL, which may affect off-target liability assessment for newer compounds
Allosteric binding sites beyond the ATP pocket and myristoyl pocket are less well characterised chemically
